This vile passion that thou hast manifested, 0 Perverse Wretch, 
will undoubtedly spread among men and women and whosoever

the sovereignty of whoever the Gods choose as their King shall

" ' Thus spoke Gautama and thereafter he reproached his

" ' " 0 Shameless One, leave my hermitage ! Though young

" ' Then Ahalya sought ro propitiate the great Risbi Gautama,

.. ' " It was in ignorance that I suffered myself ro be seduced

" ' Having spoken thus, the Rishi re-entered his hermitage,

This is why thou didst fall a victim to thy foes, 0 Vasava, and

" Hearing Bralnna's words, Mahendra undertook a sacrifice

" I have described to thee, how great was the power of

Hearing these words of Agastya, Rama and Lakshmana as

" I remember that remarkable feat now, I was formerly 
witness thereof., 
Then Rama addressed Agastya saying :-"AU thou hast said

" This, 0 Rama, is the narrative of the origin and progress of

brief.summary_1line: Brahma explains that Indra’s past seduction of Ahalya led to Gautama’s curse, causing Indra’s later humiliation and captivity by Ravana’s son Indrajit.

image_candidates.scene_text: Indrajit stands victorious on the battlefield with the chained Indra beside him as the gods watch from the sky.
Indra, disguised as the sage Gautama, enters the hermitage where the radiant Ahalya stands glowing like a flame.
The enraged sage Gautama confronts Indra in his hermitage and pronounces a terrible curse upon him.
